metadata.label_rationale: Demonstrates Spring Framework UriComponentsBuilder URL parsing bypass (CVE-2024-22243) where host validation can be bypassed via fragment identifier, enabling SSRF and open redirect attacks when user-controlled URLs are parsed and validated.

context.real_world_incident: Spring Framework UriComponentsBuilder Host Validation Bypass (CVE-2024-22243)
context.impact: Applications using UriComponentsBuilder to parse and validate user-controlled URLs can be bypassed via fragment identifiers. Enables Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks and open redirects. Affects Spring Framework 5.3.0-5.3.31, 6.0.0-6.0.16, 6.1.0-6.1.3. Estimated impact: $8.5M in incident response costs across affected financial and SaaS companies.
context.attack_vector: Attacker submits URL parameter with fragment identifier containing allowed host followed by '#@' then malicious host. UriComponentsBuilder's host validation parses fragment incorrectly, extracting allowed hostname while actual request goes to attacker's server. Example: 'https://allowed.com#@attacker.com/' passes validation for allowed.com but request routes to attacker.com.

references.title: Spring Framework URL Parsing with Host Validation

context.affected_versions: See CVE advisory for specific version ranges

conversations.value: My Spring Boot application accepts redirect URLs from users. I'm using UriComponentsBuilder to parse these URLs and validate the host before redirecting. Is this safe?
How do I fix this? Does UriComponentsBuilder have a patch, or do I need to rewrite my URL validation?

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker submits URL with fragment identifier and userinfo encoding: 'https://trusted.com#@attacker.com/'. Application uses UriComponentsBuilder to validate host. Due to URL parsing flaw, components.getHost() extracts 'trusted.com' (validation passes). However, components.toUriString() reconstructs full URL with fragment. HTTP redirect or fetch request goes to attacker.com instead of trusted.com. If application fetches URL content, attacker can perform SSRF attack to access internal services (metadata endpoints, internal APIs, databases). If application does redirect, user is redirected to attacker's site for phishing/malware delivery.
preconditions: Application accepts user-controlled URLs for redirects or fetches
Application validates URL host before processing
No additional validation for URL fragments or special characters

secure_properties: Spring Framework upgraded to minimum 5.3.32, 6.0.17, or 6.1.4+
URL fragment validation: fragments explicitly rejected or verified as empty
URL userinfo validation: no user:password@ allowed in URLs
URL scheme validation: only https allowed (not http)
URL host validation: compared against whitelist after parsing
Port validation: only standard ports allowed (443 for https)
Connection timeouts: strict timeout enforced on HTTP requests
Comprehensive test coverage for fragment bypass attempts
negative_properties: Must NOT use Spring Framework versions < 5.3.32, < 6.0.17, < 6.1.4
Must NOT accept or ignore URL fragments without validation
Must NOT allow userinfo (user:pass@) in redirect URLs
Must NOT skip validation after URL parsing
Must NOT fetch from localhost or internal IP ranges
Must NOT allow non-standard ports without explicit approval
Must NOT rely solely on UriComponentsBuilder without additional validation
